message.description: The prompt text displayed to the user, which can be plain text or formatted (e.g., with HTML or ANSI).

editing_mode.description: Sets the input editing mode to either 'emacs' (default) or 'vi', controlling key bindings and behaviour.

refresh_interval.description: Interval in seconds for refreshing the UI; useful when the prompt content updates dynamically.

vi_mode.description: Shortcut to enable Vi/Modal editing mode; equivalent to setting editing_mode='vi'.

lexer.description: Syntax highlighter (e.g., Pygments lexer) applied to the user's input as they type.

completer.description: Provides auto‑completion suggestions based on the current input, e.g., for file paths or keywords.

complete_in_thread.description: If True, runs the completion logic in a background thread to keep the UI responsive.

is_password.description: Masks user input with asterisks (or a configurable character) for secure password entry.

key_bindings.description: Custom key bindings to add or override default shortcuts for the prompt session.

bottom_toolbar.description: Text displayed in a toolbar at the bottom of the screen, useful for status messages or hints.

style.description: Custom style (colors, fonts) applied to the prompt and input area.

color_depth.description: Specifies the color depth (e.g., 1‑bit, 24‑bit) to use, overriding terminal detection.

cursor.description: Configures the shape (block, beam, underline) and blinking behaviour of the cursor.

include_default_pygments_style.description: Whether to include the default Pygments style when a lexer is used; can be a filter.

style_transformation.description: Dynamically transforms the style (e.g., to adjust contrast or invert colors) at render time.

swap_light_and_dark_colors.description: Swaps light and dark color schemes, useful for adapting to terminal background changes.

rprompt.description: Right‑aligned prompt text, often used for showing contextual information (e.g., branch name).

multiline.description: Enables multiline input, allowing the user to enter text across multiple lines.

prompt_continuation.description: Text or function that generates the continuation prompt for wrapped or continued lines.

wrap_lines.description: Whether long input lines should wrap to the next line or scroll horizontally.

enable_history_search.description: Allows the user to search through command history using the up/down arrow keys (or bindings).

search_ignore_case.description: Makes history search case‑insensitive when true.

complete_while_typing.description: Automatically shows completions as the user types, without requiring a key press (e.g., Tab).

validate_while_typing.description: Continuously validates the input as the user types and displays feedback (e.g., error indicators).

complete_style.description: Determines the appearance of the completion menu (e.g., column, scrollbar, or popup style).

auto_suggest.description: Provides a suggestion (typically from history) shown as faint text that the user can accept.

validator.description: Validates the final input; if invalid, the user is prompted to correct it before submission.

clipboard.description: Custom clipboard instance for copy/paste operations within the prompt session.

mouse_support.description: Enables mouse events (e.g., clicking to position the cursor, selecting text) in the terminal.

input_processors.description: List of processors that transform input events before they are applied to the buffer.

placeholder.description: Text shown in the input area when the buffer is empty, acting as a hint or example.

reserve_space_for_menu.description: Number of lines to reserve at the bottom of the screen for the completion menu, preventing UI jitter.

enable_system_prompt.description: If enabled, pressing Ctrl+Z suspends the application and drops to the system shell (Unix‑like).

enable_suspend.description: If enabled, allows suspending the application via the terminal's suspend key (often Ctrl+Z).

enable_open_in_editor.description: If enabled, the user can press Ctrl+E to open the current input in an external editor.

tempfile_suffix.description: Suffix (e.g., '.py') for the temporary file used when opening input in an external editor.

tempfile.description: Full path or callable returning a path for the temporary file used by the external editor.

show_frame.description: Whether to draw a visible border/frame around the input area for better visual separation.

default.description: Initial text (or Document) pre‑filled in the input buffer when the prompt is shown.

accept_default.description: If True and the user presses Enter without changing the default, the default value is accepted.

pre_run.description: Optional callback executed just before the prompt starts, useful for setup or state preparation.

set_exception_handler.description: Whether to install a custom exception handler that prints errors gracefully without crashing.

handle_sigint.description: If True, pressing Ctrl+C raises a KeyboardInterrupt; if False, SIGINT is ignored or handled differently.

in_thread.description: If True, runs the prompt in a separate thread, allowing the main thread to do other work.

inputhook.description: Hook that integrates with an event loop (e.g., asyncio, Qt, GTK) for non‑blocking input handling.
